key_record.boot_path_by_machine: no word other than the walk's own buttons appears in the record (no D-pad / A word before the first walk press in RUN 17 / RUN 18; only 0100 / 0200 in RUN 16): the runtime sent no navigation press, which is the machine's answer to how the run booted
key_record.what_it_is: the runtime's own record of WHAT IT SENT at each key change -- the link RUN 14 / RUN 15 lacked (GBP-KEY-009); with the frames it closes the join by machine at both ends (§V7.3.9)

join.definitions: HARDWARE_TESTS §V7.3.9, applied exactly: a KEY line counts only with rc=ok; the completed words in n order from 0000; R_b = the number of 0 -> 1 transitions of word bit b; the END STATE = the tally vector common to every OGBPFULL1 sample whose t_take is later than the last completed KEY line's t_done, at least two, identical; T_c = its count at counter c, blank read as 0; c(b) = the descriptor's expected key for bit b (A, B, SELECT, START, RIGHT, LEFT, UP, DOWN for bits 0..7, L for 8, R for 9)
assumptions: A1 the AGB's key lines have no source but the KEYPAD window
A2 a completed write presents its word until the next
A3 the checker's counters are edge-triggered (keysDown() at VBlank)

tally_frames.method: tools/vfull.py UNMODIFIED: load() + consumed_words() (word16 = (byte1 << 8) | byte3, raster order, GBP-VID-003); background = the word at pixel (0,0); a pixel is lit when |lum - lum(bg)| > 20 with lum = R+G+B of the 5-bit fields; the checker's tally field `%2d` at console column 22 (8x8 cells; rows 4..13 = L, R, UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT, START, SELECT, A, B); a cell is read ONLY by exact match against the glyph table below (the §V7.2.6 table, transcribed from RUN 14 / RUN 15's frames); an unknown bitmap aborts the reading
tally_frames.classification: FACT (data, recomputable): the preserved OGBPFULL1 frames of this run show the checker's tally screen with counts equal to the walk's arithmetic expectation, reproducible from the archived file with the frozen parser -- NOT operator observation. With the KEY record (this run's own), the frames are one of the two machine ends of the join.
